newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean union backs down on full strike call.
newsitem.headline: South Korean union backs down on full strike call.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed union body on Wednesday backed away from its call for all-out public sector stoppages, instead urging partial strikes in key services as well as industrial walkouts.

"We are deeply concerned about the difficulties and worries to ordinary citizens and have decided to modulate strikes in the public sector," Kwon Young-kil, head of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, told a news conference.
Lee Sang-hyun, the confederation's chief organiser, told Reuters the union would temporarily suspend most of its public sector strikes from Friday.
"From Friday, only broadcasters and manufacturers will be on an indefinite strike," he said.

Kwon and others leaders of the confederation have been directing three weeks of wildcat stoppages from the sanctuary of a Seoul cathedral in protest at a controversial new labour law rammed through parliament on December 26.
The conferation and the officially-sanctioned Federation of Korean Trade Unions had urged their members to observe "all-out" stoppages on Wednesday but workers have largely ignored the call.
